evidence.note: Early plans name most subsystems (CLI dev/build/start, SSR server, next/* shims, route scanning, middleware, SSG) and construction proceeds in a rough dependency order: package.json -> runtime -> shims -> index/plugin -> server -> CLI. Shows subsystem identification and coarse ordering, but as a bundled build, not sequenced milestones.

All subsystems are written monolithically before any verification; the first check (step 15) is the full 335-test suite rather than a thin vertical slice (one route under dev) gated before layering. No incremental subsystem done-criteria.

Post-build work is reactive, failure-driven patching loosely prioritized by 'highest remaining broad gap' (config -> metadata -> cookies -> hydration). Demonstrates impact-based ordering and subsystem awareness, but no maintained milestone plan or explicit done-criteria.
Late routing bug (root app/page mapped to /page) and repeated submit-complete/resume cycles show continued whack-a-mole with no re-planned milestone boundaries or through-line decomposition.

reasoning: The agent clearly identifies the major subsystems and constructs them in a coarse dependency order (shims/resolution -> server -> CLI -> build -> tests), and during fixing it prioritizes by broad impact — matching aspects of anchor 5. But it never establishes a thin, verified end-to-end slice before piling features on, front-loads a monolithic build gated only by the full suite, and maintains no explicit milestones, done-criteria, or revisited decomposition, keeping it below anchor 5 and well short of anchor 8. This places it at a 4, between the generic-list anchor (3) and the sensible-ordering-with-done-notions anchor (5).
